beats.text: One spoon of ice cream. And your forehead explodes.
In a study published in the BMJ, students ate ice cream either fast, or slowly.
Eating fast? About twenty-seven percent got a brain freeze. Slowly? About twelve.
The cold hits the roof of your mouth. But the pain shows up in your forehead.
The fix: press your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Warm it up.
So your brain isn't freezing. The pain just went to the wrong address.

sources: Kaczorowski & Kaczorowski (2002). Ice cream evoked headaches (ICE-H) study: randomised trial of accelerated versus cautious ice cream eating regimen. BMJ 325. Under 5 s: 27% headache; over 30 s: 12%.
Mechanism: palate cold -> trigeminal nerve -> referred pain in forehead. Via Wikipedia 'Cold-stimulus headache'.
